children: is preparing a major expansion of its same-day delivery infrastructure in the US that could significantly increase the reach of its rapid-delivery network.
The initiative, known internally as Project Mercury, would grow Amazon’s same-day fulfillment footprint to more than 1,000 sites by 2031, up from about 85 currently,
reported, citing internal planning documents. The expansion would give Amazon a larger network of facilities positioned closer to customers for faster deliveries.

According to the documents, Amazon plans to reconfigure its same-day delivery footprint around much shorter distances between facilities and customers. While the company currently locates same-day sites roughly a 90-minute drive from customers, the project aims to place those facilities within a 10-mile straight-line radius of 80% of US Prime subscribers by 2031.

Amazon’s finance team has also evaluated the economics of Project Mercury, with operations chief Udit Madan involved in the planning, according to the report. The company’s three-year operating plan allocates $6.8B for US same-day delivery capacity in 2026 and 2027.

A separate internal analysis estimated the project could generate $7.1B in economic value over a decade and reach positive cash flow by 2030, while some of the investment could replace spending on traditional delivery facilities.
An Amazon spokesperson told Business Insider that internal projections are "preliminary, subject to significant revision, and shouldn't be treated as finalized plans."
The company said its same-day service already reaches more than 10,000 cities and towns, including rural areas, although not all same-day orders are handled through dedicated same-day facilities.

"That said, it's no secret that we're focused on delivering faster for customers and the expansion of our same-day delivery network is playing a big role in that," the spokesperson said. "We continue to invest in fast delivery speed and convenience alongside wide selection and everyday low prices."

title: Amazon targets 1K same-day delivery hubs by 2031: report
